problems.title: Inlining can call the wrong method for an abstract type argument
problems.summary: On Julia 1.10, union-splitting a call with a Type{<:T} argument can select a method that does not accept the value. Julia 1.11 fixed this in the compiler. This commit backports the fix and its regression test to 1.10. Julia PR #64529 proposes the same backport for 1.10.

fix.why_together: The upstream guard relies on removing the earlier unmatched-parameter shortcut. One commit carries both changes to compute_inlining_cases and the regression test.

problems.title: A one-index request can return the other eigenvalue of a 2×2 tridiagonal matrix
problems.summary: For a symmetric tridiagonal matrix with negative trace, eigmin, eigmax and a one-index range can select the wrong eigenvalue. LAPACK 3.12 fixed xSTEMR. This branch adopts the corrected OpenBLAS binary for Julia 1.10.

commits.title: Use the OpenBLAS_jll 0.3.34+1 binary artifact: its LAPACK 3.12 fixes xSTEMR for 2x2 index ranges (Reference-LAPACK/lapack#826)

fix.why_together: The OpenBLAS_jll version and artifact checksums must agree for the build to download and verify the binary.

requires.why: This commit updates the BinaryBuilder artifact used by the Julia build. Compiling OpenBLAS from source still uses the separate source pin.

validation.detail: The LAPACK #826 probe returned the correct eigenvalues.

problems.title: Julia can hang in a waiting exit hook after SIGTERM
problems.summary: During shutdown, a hook that waits for I/O or a timer can stall on a runtime lock left held by the interrupted task. Julia 1.11 releases those locks before running the hooks. This is the 1.10 backport.

commits.title: Backport d8a410c8eb (#51849) to v1.10.12: release the locks of the task an abrupt exit interrupts, so SIGTERM exit hooks that wait cannot deadlock on libuv's lock

fix.why_together: The signal-handling change from upstream commit d8a410c8eb releases the interrupted task’s locks as its stack is discarded.

tests: Waiting exit hook on SIGTERM
validation.detail: The exit hook completed and the child process exited within the probe’s deadline.

tests: Waiting exit hook on SIGTERM
validation.detail: The waiting exit hook completed after SIGTERM within the probe’s deadline.

tests: Julia #51849 shutdown probe and atexit tests
validation.detail: The waiting exit hook completed during signal-driven shutdown.

problems.title: A cancelled stream read can deadlock Julia
problems.summary: Cleanup after an interrupted pipe, socket or TTY read can acquire the stream condition and libuv locks in the opposite order from a read callback. The fork uses a consistent order in both read paths. Julia tracks the problem in #64934.

commits.title: Fix the lock order of wait_readnb and readuntil after an interrupted wait: take the iolock before the stream condition, as libuv read callbacks do, so the teardown cannot deadlock against one

fix.why_together: Both wait_readnb and readuntil stop the active read during cleanup and need the same lock order.

tests: Stream lock ordering after an interrupted read
validation.detail: The lock-order check observed cleanup acquire the locks in the expected order.

tests: Stream lock ordering after an interrupted read
validation.detail: The interrupted read acquired the libuv and stream locks in the expected order.

tests: Interrupted stream-read probe and read/spawn suites
validation.detail: The interrupted reader completed cleanup, and the read and process tests passed.

problems.title: Different checkouts of one package wait on the same precompile lock
problems.summary: Two Julia processes with a shared depot can queue behind one lock even when their source paths differ and the second process must compile again. The fork keys both the lock and the cache slot on the source path. Upstream tracks this in #51850.

commits.title: Key the package compile lock and cache file name on the source file, so two checkouts of one package compile at the same time and never write one cache file (JuliaLang/julia#51850)

fix.why_together: Separating only the locks would let the two compilers write the same cache file. The lock and output names change together.

tests: Concurrent precompilation with separate and shared package sources
validation.detail: Separate checkouts overlapped by 3.05 s. Two environments sharing one source compiled it once. Separate sources in one environment retained distinct cache files.

tests: Concurrent precompilation with separate and shared package sources
validation.detail: All three checks passed. Two checkouts compiled with 3.01 s of overlap, one shared source compiled once, and separate sources kept separate cache files.

tests: Concurrent package precompilation in separate checkouts
validation.detail: The three cases passed for parallel checkouts, reuse of one source from two environments and separate cache files for two sources in one environment.

problems.title: Rebuilding a package can remove a cache image a running Julia session still needs
problems.summary: When a package is rebuilt, a running session may lose the dependency image needed to compile another package. Julia master fixed this with per-build cache files and advisory locks. This commit backports that design to 1.10.

commits.title: Backport JuliaLang/julia#63539 and #63613: name cache files by build and retain images used by running sessions

fix.why_together: Build-specific names prevent replacement. Loaded-image locks and pruning determine which generations may be removed. This backport preserves the source-keyed slots introduced by the preceding fix.

tests: Cache generation retention, eviction and retry
validation.detail: All 10 checks passed, covering concurrent builds, edited dependencies, a disappeared image and retention on filesystems without locking.

tests: Cache generation retention, eviction and retry
validation.detail: All 10 checks passed, covering concurrent builds, edited dependencies, a missing image and retention without filesystem locking.

problems.title: Repeated deep stack walks evict their own unwind information
problems.summary: On Linux and FreeBSD, Julia 1.10 uses a libunwind cache of 128 entries. Deep stack walks can evict entries needed on the next throw or sample. The fork requests 4096 entries at startup. Julia tracks this in #65052.

commits.title: Enlarge libunwind's register-state cache to 4096 entries at start, so a stack walk from a deep stack hits the cache instead of looking every frame up again under the cache's lock

fix.why_together: Runtime initialization creates the libunwind cache and then sets its size before other threads begin using it.

tests: Deep-throw timing with the shipped cache and the 128-entry setting
validation.detail: On x86-64 Linux with 428 stack entries, a deep throw took 79.7 µs as shipped and 577.4 µs after restoring 128 entries in the same process (7.2×).

tests: Deep-throw timing with the shipped cache and the 128-entry setting
validation.detail: On x86-64 Linux, a throw with 428 stack entries took 107.8 µs with the shipped cache and 676.0 µs after restoring the 128-entry setting in the same process.

tests: Deep-throw benchmark with the shipped and default unwind caches
validation.detail: At 428 frames, a throw took 233.2 µs as shipped and 1490.7 µs with the original cache size restored.

problems.title: Large buffered stream reads can fail with EINVAL on macOS
problems.summary: When a pipe, socket or TTY has more than 2 GiB of receive-buffer space, Julia 1.10 can request a read larger than macOS accepts. The fork caps each native read and lets the stream continue reading the rest.

draft.title: Large buffered stream reads can fail with EINVAL on macOS
draft.body: A Julia 1.10 stream on macOS can have more buffer space available than the operating system accepts in a single read. A socket or pipe with that much room can fail with EINVAL during an otherwise ordinary transfer. Limiting each request to INT_MAX preserves the connection and lets subsequent reads fill the rest of the buffer. The macOS arm64 build passed checks at and on either side of that limit.

commits.title: Cap each native stream read at INT_MAX bytes on macOS, as on Windows: macOS's read(2) fails with EINVAL above it

fix.why_together: One change limits the length offered to libuv on macOS. Linux keeps its normal read length.

tests: Native stream read-length boundary checks
validation.detail: The macOS binary passed the read-length check on both sides of the signed 32-bit limit.

tests: Linux stream read-length checks
validation.detail: Linux preserved the requested read length. The macOS boundary result was measured separately on the 1.10.12 build.

problems.title: Loading a package image can attach an invoke dependency to the wrong method
problems.summary: Two callers can share an invoke signature while depending on different specializations. Julia 1.10 can restore both dependencies onto one callee, leaving a caller with stale code after its own callee changes.

draft.title: Loading a package image can attach an invoke dependency to the wrong method
draft.body: On Julia 1.10, loading a package from its compiled image can change which method redefinition invalidates one of its callers. Two invoke sites may have the same signature object and select different callees. Both should behave as they do when loaded from source. Keeping the callee identity when deduplicating serialized dependencies restored that behavior in a two-caller comparison.

commits.title: Key a package image's invoke targets by signature and callee, so callers sharing one invoke signature object keep their own callee on load

fix.why_together: One change to package-image serialization distinguishes the callee as well as the signature. Rebuilding a package image records both dependencies correctly.

tests: Method invalidation after loading from source and a package image
validation.detail: Each caller kept its expected callee, both when loaded from source and when restored from an image.

tests: Compare invoke dependencies loaded from source and from an image
validation.detail: Each caller retained its own callee in both modes.

problems.title: A process that waited for a pidfile can retain a watcher after acquiring the lock
problems.summary: A short-lived Julia 1.10 process can wait for the polling timeout during shutdown after briefly contending for a pidfile. The backport closes the watcher when the wait finishes.

commits.title: Backport the pidfile half of b6e013646639 to v1.10.12: watch for the lock in the waiting task and close the watcher before returning, so a process that waited for a pidfile lock does not keep a file watcher running

fix.why_together: The pidfile part of Julia #55877 closes the watcher and timer in the waiting task. It applies without the broader FileMonitor rewrite.

tests: Precompile worker waiting on a held pidfile
validation.detail: The worker exited successfully in 0.9 s after waiting for a lock held for 0.5 s. The watcher check found no pending wait.

tests: Worker acquiring a contended pidfile
validation.detail: The worker finished with no watcher left running.

problems.title: Opaque closures can fail to capture an enclosing method’s static parameters
problems.summary: Julia 1.10 can terminate while constructing an opaque closure that refers to a static parameter of the surrounding method. Julia #57928 fixed the lowering on newer releases. The public 1.10 backport and the fleet commit carry the same patch.

fix.why_together: The single backport includes the lowering change and its regression tests. The original and the prepared commit are alternative applications of that patch.

problems.title: Julia 1.10 collects much more frequently after the live heap exceeds roughly 2.3 GiB
problems.summary: A Julia 1.10 process can spend more time in GC when the same allocation workload retains a slightly larger heap. The collector falls back to its small default interval once half the live size exceeds its maximum interval.

draft.title: Julia 1.10 collects much more frequently after the live heap exceeds roughly 2.3 GiB
draft.body: A Julia 1.10 allocation workload becomes much more expensive to collect after the live heap passes about 2.3 GiB. Half the live size has then reached the upper limit for the next allocation interval, but the collector selects its small default instead. The expected behavior is to keep the upper limit. With that change the large-heap check needed ten collections, all incremental. A process with less headroom can also lower the interval cap.

commits.title: Keep the collection interval at max_collect_interval once half the live heap exceeds it, instead of falling back to the default, and let JULIA_KB_GC_MAX_INTERVAL_MB set that maximum for one process

fix.why_together: The commit clamps the interval at its maximum and allows a process to lower the cap to fit its available memory. Julia 1.11 uses different heuristics.

tests: Fixed allocation workload with different collection limits and a large live heap
validation.detail: The large-heap case used ten collections, with no full collections. The configured cap, minimum and invalid-value checks passed.

tests: Collection-interval checks and Julia gc test suite
validation.detail: The large-heap case completed with ten collections, none full. The configured cap, floor and invalid-value checks passed.

problems.title: JIT stack unwinding can fail on Julia 1.10 for AArch64 Linux
problems.summary: Julia 1.10 on AArch64 Linux uses LLVM 15 to link JIT code. Its unwind metadata can be incomplete for the platform unwinder. The fork supplies the table terminator provided by newer LLVM versions.

draft.title: JIT stack unwinding can fail on Julia 1.10 for AArch64 Linux
draft.body: On AArch64 Linux with Julia 1.10 and LLVM 15, unwinding JIT-generated code can terminate the process. The ELF unwind tables should carry the terminator expected by the platform unwinder. The fork applies the convention used by newer LLVM versions and passes the native AArch64 regression check. The change is specific to that object format and architecture. [Upstream LLVM change](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/68c14f582ce64ae6bd79e78b609fa3469af0ed83)

commits.title: End each JIT unwind table with a zero length word on ELF/aarch64, as LLVM 16 does (D146067), so libgcc never reads past a table that ends at its page end

fix.why_together: The single JITLink change applies only to ELF on AArch64 and completes each unwind table before registration. The upstream LLVM change is D146067.

tests: JIT unwind-table regression check on the native AArch64 build
validation.detail: The platform-specific regression passed in the native build of the original 1.10.12 patch.

tests: AArch64 JIT unwind-table regression
validation.detail: This merged build ran on x86-64. The native AArch64 result above covers the original 1.10.12 fix.
